newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss say Zaireans demand freeze of Mobutu assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss say Zaireans demand freeze of Mobutu assets.

text.p: Switzerland said on Wednesday that Zairean prosecutors had filed a request for Swiss authorities to freeze the assets of Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko in the Alpine country.

A brief government statement said president Arnold Koller on Wednesday informed the cabinet of the Zairean demand, received on Tuesday. "As is usual in such cases, this request will be reviewed by the responsible departments (Justice and Foreign Ministries)," the statement said.
The Swiss Foreign Ministry has repeatedly said it would consider freezing the funds of Mobutu in the country only if a request came from Zairean authorities.
Rebels who are marching on Zaire's capital of Kinshasa and have vowed to topple the cancer-stricken Mobutu, have already asked Switzerland to freeze Mobutu's wealth here.

Swiss media estimate Mobutu's fortune to total about $4 billion spread among secret bank accounts in Switzerland, where he also owns a luxury villa in Lausanne and his son has had various business dealings.

The Federal Banking Commission, the country's top banking watchdog, promised to widen a search for the funds on Tuesday after saying a previous informal check among leading banks had found no trace of any money.
